goal: Help the developer configure non-Store App Installer updates so launch-time checks work on supported Windows versions.
must_include: Identifies that the `.appinstaller` file uses the older `http://schemas.microsoft.com/appx/appinstaller/2017/2` namespace while the desired launch update settings require the 2018 App Installer schema.
Changes the root namespace to `http://schemas.microsoft.com/appx/appinstaller/2018` and keeps `UpdateSettings` with `OnLaunch HoursBetweenUpdateChecks="0"` for every-launch checks.
Mentions the relevant Windows version support: `OnLaunch` starts at Windows 10 1709 and `HoursBetweenUpdateChecks` at 1803; prompt/blocking options are 1903+ if they are later added.
Checks that the installed app's App Installer URI and the `MainBundle` URI/version/publisher point to the updated, reachable HTTPS files.
must_not: Says MSIX can only auto-update through the Microsoft Store.
Blames the `_Test` folder suffix by itself when the URI still points at the actual bundle location.
Suggests switching to ClickOnce as the only way to get launch-time update checks.
acceptable_alternatives: Use `AutomaticBackgroundTask` instead of or in addition to `OnLaunch` if silent background checks are acceptable.
Use Visual Studio's update-settings dialog to regenerate the App Installer file with the newer schema.
Use `PackageManager`/enterprise deployment tooling to update devices directly if App Installer launch checks are unsuitable.
solved: The answer updates the App Installer schema/settings and verifies version/URI/publisher prerequisites for the sideload update feed.
partial: The answer mentions update settings or Windows version support but misses the old schema namespace in the fixture.
notes: The source answer centers on the 2018 namespace. Windows version details are included so graders accept answers that also check whether the target OS supports the selected update settings.
